Extra slice functions for a PlySummarizedExperiment

Source: R/dplyr-slice_extras.R
slice_extras.Rd

Convenience wrappers around slice() that select rows and/or columns of a PlySummarizedExperiment object:

  • slice_min() and slice_max() select the rows or columns with the smallest or largest values of a variable.

  • slice_head() and slice_tail() select the first or last rows or columns.

  • slice_sample() randomly samples rows and/or columns, optionally weighted by a variable.

Unlike their data.frame counterparts, every one of these verbs uses the rows() and cols() context functions within ... to declare which dimension(s) of the object are sliced. If an object is grouped, slicing happens within each group of the respective context.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'PlySummarizedExperiment'
slice_max(.data, ..., n = NULL, prop = NULL, with_ties = TRUE, na_rm = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'PlySummarizedExperiment'
slice_min(.data, ..., n = NULL, prop = NULL, with_ties = TRUE, na_rm = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'PlySummarizedExperiment'
slice_head(.data, ..., n = NULL, prop = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'PlySummarizedExperiment'
slice_tail(.data, ..., n = NULL, prop = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'PlySummarizedExperiment'
slice_sample(
  .data,
  ...,
  n = NULL,
  prop = NULL,
  weight_by = NULL,
  replace = FALSE
)

Arguments

.data

a PlySummarizedExperiment object.

...

calls to the rows() and/or cols() context functions. The assays() context is not available for slicing. The meaning of the context contents depends on the verb:

  • slice_min()/slice_max(): an expression giving the variable to order by within that context, e.g. rows(length).

  • slice_head()/slice_tail(): must be empty, e.g. rows() or cols(). They only indicate which context(s) to slice.

  • slice_sample(): either empty, indicating a uniform sample of that context, or an expression, which is used as the weight_by value for that context.

n, prop

Provide either n, the number of rows/columns, or prop, the proportion of rows/columns to select (per group). If neither is supplied, n = 1 is used. Supplying both is an error.

A negative value of n or prop is subtracted from the group size, i.e. n = -2 keeps all but 2 rows/columns. Positive values are rounded down, negative values rounded up, and the result is truncated to the group size (unless slice_sample(replace = TRUE)).

Always pass n/prop by name. Some calls error if they are left unnamed or omitted; see the section "Naming n and prop" below.

with_ties

Should ties be kept together? The default, TRUE, may return more rows/columns than requested. Use FALSE to return exactly n rows/columns, with ties broken by position.

na_rm

Should missing values be removed? The default, FALSE, ranks NA values last, so they are only kept when there are not enough non-missing values to satisfy n/prop. If TRUE, missing values are never selected.

weight_by

Sampling weights wrapped in a context function, such as rows(foo) or cols(bar). Each value must be non-negative. This is an alternative to giving a non-empty context in ...; only one weight may be specified per context.

replace

Should sampling be performed with (TRUE) or without (FALSE, the default) replacement? When TRUE, n/prop may exceed the group size.

Value

a PlySummarizedExperiment object.

Details

Naming n and prop

Before dispatching to the methods, the dplyr generics check that n was not passed by position. If neither n nor prop is supplied, they error when exactly one unnamed argument is left in .... For slice_min()/slice_max(), the first context fills the generic's order_by argument. As a result, either the rows() or the cols() context can be used on its own, but they can only be used together when n or prop is named. In other words, the following does not work:

slice_min(xp, rows(foo), cols(bar))

but either of the following does:

slice_min(xp, rows(foo), cols(bar), n = 1)

xp |>
  slice_min(rows(foo)) |>
  slice_min(cols(bar))

Likewise, slice_head(), slice_tail() and slice_sample() need n or prop to be named when only a single context is supplied, e.g. slice_head(xp, rows(), n = 1) rather than slice_head(xp, rows()).

slice_head()/slice_tail()

For a data.frame, these generics do not use the ... argument. For PlySummarizedExperiment objects, ... specifies the rows() and/or cols() contexts to slice, and these expressions must be empty:

slice_head(xp, rows(), n = 1)
slice_tail(xp, cols(), n = 1)
slice_head(xp, rows(), cols(), n = 2)

slice_sample()

As with slice_head()/slice_tail(), empty context calls indicate which contexts to sample. A non-empty context is used as the weight_by argument for that context:

# uniform sample of both
slice_sample(xp, rows(), cols(), n = 2)
# weight rows by `foo`, and cols by `bar`
slice_sample(xp, rows(foo), cols(bar), n = 2)
# weight rows by `foo`, uniform cols
slice_sample(xp, rows(foo), cols(), n = 2)
# weight rows by `foo`, using the `weight_by` argument
slice_sample(xp, weight_by = rows(foo), n = 2)

See also

slice(), dplyr::slice_min(), dplyr::slice_head(), dplyr::slice_sample()

Examples

# slice_min() / slice_max() ---------------------------------------
slice_max(se_simple, rows(length), n = 2)
#> # A SummarizedExperiment-tibble Abstraction: 2 × 4
#>   .features .samples | counts logcounts | gene  length direction | sample
#>   <chr>     <chr>    |  <int>     <dbl> | <chr>  <int> <chr>     | <chr> 
#> 1 row_3     col_1    |     16      2.77 | g3        60 +         | s1    
#> 2 row_4     col_1    |     11      2.40 | g4        39 -         | s1    
#> 3 row_3     col_2    |      6      1.79 | g3        60 +         | s2    
#> 4 row_4     col_2    |     17      2.83 | g4        39 -         | s2    
#> 5 row_3     col_3    |     15      2.71 | g3        60 +         | s3    
#> 6 row_4     col_3    |     10      2.30 | g4        39 -         | s3    
#> 7 row_3     col_4    |     20      3.00 | g3        60 +         | s4    
#> 8 row_4     col_4    |      3      1.10 | g4        39 -         | s4    
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: condition <chr>
slice_min(se_simple, cols(sample))
#> # A SummarizedExperiment-tibble Abstraction: 5 × 1
#>   .features .samples | counts logcounts | gene  length direction | sample
#>   <chr>     <chr>    |  <int>     <dbl> | <chr>  <int> <chr>     | <chr> 
#> 1 row_1     col_1    |     14      2.64 | g1         1 -         | s1    
#> 2 row_2     col_1    |     19      2.94 | g2        24 +         | s1    
#> 3 row_3     col_1    |     16      2.77 | g3        60 +         | s1    
#> 4 row_4     col_1    |     11      2.40 | g4        39 -         | s1    
#> 5 row_5     col_1    |     18      2.89 | g5        37 +         | s1    
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: condition <chr>
# name `n` when using both contexts
slice_min(se_simple, rows(length), cols(sample), n = 1)
#> # A SummarizedExperiment-tibble Abstraction: 1 × 1
#>   .features .samples | counts logcounts | gene  length direction | sample
#>   <chr>     <chr>    |  <int>     <dbl> | <chr>  <int> <chr>     | <chr> 
#> 1 row_1     col_1    |     14      2.64 | g1         1 -         | s1    
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: condition <chr>

gse <- group_by(se_simple, rows(direction))
slice_max(gse, rows(length), n = 1)
#> # A SummarizedExperiment-tibble Abstraction: 2 × 4
#> # Groups: rows(direction)
#>   .features .samples | counts logcounts | direction gene  length | sample
#>   <chr>     <chr>    |  <int>     <dbl> | <chr>     <chr>  <int> | <chr> 
#> 1 row_4     col_1    |     11      2.40 | -         g4        39 | s1    
#> 2 row_3     col_1    |     16      2.77 | +         g3        60 | s1    
#> 3 row_4     col_2    |     17      2.83 | -         g4        39 | s2    
#> 4 row_3     col_2    |      6      1.79 | +         g3        60 | s2    
#> 5 row_4     col_3    |     10      2.30 | -         g4        39 | s3    
#> 6 row_3     col_3    |     15      2.71 | +         g3        60 | s3    
#> 7 row_4     col_4    |      3      1.10 | -         g4        39 | s4    
#> 8 row_3     col_4    |     20      3.00 | +         g3        60 | s4    
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: condition <chr>

# slice_head() / slice_tail() -------------------------------------
slice_head(se_simple, rows(), n = 1)
#> # A SummarizedExperiment-tibble Abstraction: 1 × 4
#>   .features .samples | counts logcounts | gene  length direction | sample
#>   <chr>     <chr>    |  <int>     <dbl> | <chr>  <int> <chr>     | <chr> 
#> 1 row_1     col_1    |     14      2.64 | g1         1 -         | s1    
#> 2 row_1     col_2    |      8      2.08 | g1         1 -         | s2    
#> 3 row_1     col_3    |      7      1.95 | g1         1 -         | s3    
#> 4 row_1     col_4    |      9      2.20 | g1         1 -         | s4    
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: condition <chr>
slice_tail(se_simple, cols(), n = 2)
#> # A SummarizedExperiment-tibble Abstraction: 5 × 2
#>    .features .samples | counts logcounts | gene  length direction | sample
#>    <chr>     <chr>    |  <int>     <dbl> | <chr>  <int> <chr>     | <chr> 
#>  1 row_1     col_3    |      7      1.95 | g1         1 -         | s3    
#>  2 row_2     col_3    |      1      0    | g2        24 +         | s3    
#>  3 row_3     col_3    |     15      2.71 | g3        60 +         | s3    
#>  4 row_4     col_3    |     10      2.30 | g4        39 -         | s3    
#>  5 row_5     col_3    |     12      2.48 | g5        37 +         | s3    
#>  6 row_1     col_4    |      9      2.20 | g1         1 -         | s4    
#>  7 row_2     col_4    |      4      1.39 | g2        24 +         | s4    
#>  8 row_3     col_4    |     20      3.00 | g3        60 +         | s4    
#>  9 row_4     col_4    |      3      1.10 | g4        39 -         | s4    
#> 10 row_5     col_4    |      5      1.61 | g5        37 +         | s4    
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: condition <chr>
# negative `n` drops rows: all but the last 2
slice_head(se_simple, rows(), n = -2)
#> # A SummarizedExperiment-tibble Abstraction: 3 × 4
#>     .features .samples | counts logcounts | gene  length direction | sample
#>     <chr>     <chr>    |  <int>     <dbl> | <chr>  <int> <chr>     | <chr> 
#>   1 row_1     col_1    |     14     2.64  | g1         1 -         | s1    
#>   2 row_2     col_1    |     19     2.94  | g2        24 +         | s1    
#>   3 row_3     col_1    |     16     2.77  | g3        60 +         | s1    
#>   4 row_1     col_2    |      8     2.08  | g1         1 -         | s2    
#>   5 row_2     col_2    |      2     0.693 | g2        24 +         | s2    
#>   …   …         …             …       …      …         … …            …    
#> n-4 row_2     col_3    |      1     0     | g2        24 +         | s3    
#> n-3 row_3     col_3    |     15     2.71  | g3        60 +         | s3    
#> n-2 row_1     col_4    |      9     2.20  | g1         1 -         | s4    
#> n-1 row_2     col_4    |      4     1.39  | g2        24 +         | s4    
#> n   row_3     col_4    |     20     3.00  | g3        60 +         | s4    
#> # ℹ n = 12
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: condition <chr>
slice_head(se_simple, rows(), cols(), n = 2)
#> # A SummarizedExperiment-tibble Abstraction: 2 × 2
#>   .features .samples | counts logcounts | gene  length direction | sample
#>   <chr>     <chr>    |  <int>     <dbl> | <chr>  <int> <chr>     | <chr> 
#> 1 row_1     col_1    |     14     2.64  | g1         1 -         | s1    
#> 2 row_2     col_1    |     19     2.94  | g2        24 +         | s1    
#> 3 row_1     col_2    |      8     2.08  | g1         1 -         | s2    
#> 4 row_2     col_2    |      2     0.693 | g2        24 +         | s2    
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: condition <chr>

# slice_sample() --------------------------------------------------
set.seed(1)
slice_sample(se_simple, rows(), cols(), n = 2)
#> # A SummarizedExperiment-tibble Abstraction: 2 × 2
#>   .features .samples | counts logcounts | gene  length direction | sample
#>   <chr>     <chr>    |  <int>     <dbl> | <chr>  <int> <chr>     | <chr> 
#> 1 row_1     col_1    |     14      2.64 | g1         1 -         | s1    
#> 2 row_2     col_1    |     19      2.94 | g2        24 +         | s1    
#> 3 row_1     col_3    |      7      1.95 | g1         1 -         | s3    
#> 4 row_2     col_3    |      1      0    | g2        24 +         | s3    
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: condition <chr>
slice_sample(se_simple, rows(length), cols(), n = 2)
#> # A SummarizedExperiment-tibble Abstraction: 2 × 2
#>   .features .samples | counts logcounts | gene  length direction | sample
#>   <chr>     <chr>    |  <int>     <dbl> | <chr>  <int> <chr>     | <chr> 
#> 1 row_5     col_1    |     18      2.89 | g5        37 +         | s1    
#> 2 row_4     col_1    |     11      2.40 | g4        39 -         | s1    
#> 3 row_5     col_3    |     12      2.48 | g5        37 +         | s3    
#> 4 row_4     col_3    |     10      2.30 | g4        39 -         | s3    
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: condition <chr>
slice_sample(se_simple, weight_by = rows(length), n = 2)
#> # A SummarizedExperiment-tibble Abstraction: 2 × 4
#>   .features .samples | counts logcounts | gene  length direction | sample
#>   <chr>     <chr>    |  <int>     <dbl> | <chr>  <int> <chr>     | <chr> 
#> 1 row_3     col_1    |     16      2.77 | g3        60 +         | s1    
#> 2 row_4     col_1    |     11      2.40 | g4        39 -         | s1    
#> 3 row_3     col_2    |      6      1.79 | g3        60 +         | s2    
#> 4 row_4     col_2    |     17      2.83 | g4        39 -         | s2    
#> 5 row_3     col_3    |     15      2.71 | g3        60 +         | s3    
#> 6 row_4     col_3    |     10      2.30 | g4        39 -         | s3    
#> 7 row_3     col_4    |     20      3.00 | g3        60 +         | s4    
#> 8 row_4     col_4    |      3      1.10 | g4        39 -         | s4    
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: condition <chr>
